vedic_reference.note: Vaivasvat is a name of Manu, the progenitor of the human race. He is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures.

data.cultural_impact: Manu, the first human being on earth and the protagonist of the Hindu epic Mahabharata, is popularly known by the name Vaivasvat. He is so named because he was born when the god Savitri (another name for the Sun God) entered the womb of his mother, Shatarudi, after her long penance to have a child. The name Vaivasvat signifies the divine descent of Manu from the Sun God, emphasizing his divine ancestry, and highlighting the unique place of Manu in Hindu mythology as the progenitor of the human race.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, Vaivasvat's name signifies the eternal connection between the divine cosmic order (Dharma) and human civilization. As the Law-giver and the first human being, Manu laid down the foundation for social and moral values in human society, paving the way for Dharma, or righteous living. By carrying the divine name Vaivasvat, Manu represented the eternal embodiment of Dharma, embodying the divine tradition that has shaped the spiritual and cultural evolution of the Hindu civilization. In this context, the name Vaivasvat stands as a reminder of the ultimate goal of human life, which is to live in harmony with the divine cosmic order and attain spiritual liberation.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu sage and king Vaivasvat Manu is believed to be the author of the ancient Indian legal text, the Manusmriti. Manu's work is considered a foundational text in Hindu society.
historical_references.context: Manusmriti is one of the oldest known texts in Hinduism, detailing laws, customs, and social structure as per Hindu dharma.

historical_references.reference: Vaivasvat is also known as the progenitor of the solar dynasty in Hindu mythology. He was the son of the god Vivasvat and his wife Saranyu.
historical_references.context: Vaivasvat is an important figure in Hindu mythology, considered the founder of the solar dynasty.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name "Vaivasvat" has gained modern relevance across various platforms, most notably in Astrology, Spacetech, and Mythology. In the Astrology community, Vaivasvat is known as the name of the legendary king Manu in Hindu mythology, believed to have started the first human civilization. Instagram influencers and astrologers frequently use the name in their posts and stories to engage their followers. The term "Vaivasvat Manu" hashtag sees significant usage with over 100,000 posts. In the Spacetech sector, ISRO's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) is named after Vaivasvat, the Sun God in Hindu mythology. The scientific and technological community often uses the name in discussions related to space exploration and satellite launches. Finally, in the Mythology community, Vaivasvat is a popular character, and cosplayers and artists often showcase their creative interpretations of the character on platforms like Twitter and Reddit, leading to widespread engagement and trending topics.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Vaivasvat signifies the eternal and supreme sun god, Surya. It represents the radiant and infinite source of light and life, guiding us through the cycles of time.

seo.description_paragraph: Vaivasvat, also known as Manu, is an ancient Sanskrit name rooted in Hinduism. The name Vaivasvat is derived from the Sanskrit word 'vaivasva', which means 'all-pervading' or 'omnipresent'. In Hindu mythology, Vaivasvat is considered as the name of the first man, Manu, who is the son of the Sun God. This name carries significant cultural and religious value in Hinduism.
